description: Must-run end-to-end scenarios (docs/test-plan/04-e2e-test-plan.md §3). Factor values not listed take `defaults`. Lanes: Es-PR (scripted, gating on PR), Es-nightly (scripted, nightly), El-release (live models, budgeted, per release), K8s-kind, Iso-gVisor, Iso-Kata (runners the default CI lacks).

scenarios.title: R31-SECKEY: no org or platform credential enters an engine sandbox, no upstream is reachable from one but through the gateways, and a sandbox's tokens reach only its run's grants
steps: On a human-style stack, canaries are planted where the product keeps every kind of credential (deployment/e2e/seckey_inventory.py, held to the code's enumerations by tests/cohesion/test_r31seckey_canary_inventory.py): a stored model per LLM and embedding provider, MCP servers signed in by API token, header and OAuth (access, refresh, client secret), every keyed web search provider and SearXNG (live), Jira Data Center (live), OAuth and basic-auth toolset sign-ins, and every secret in the stack's and the platform containers' environments.

On every release engine (engines.py kinds), two jobs of an agent with all of them: one holds before its first call, one after every credential-bearing call; each calls four MCP servers, the Jira toolset and web search.
expect_user: Each job ends with its answer and every tool's result (SK-5).
assert_journal: SK-1..SK-3: no canary in raw, base64, percent-encoded or hex form in any file, environment or command line of the live sandbox (sentinels prove /tmp, /state, /workspace and environments were read); no credential shape; credential-named variables hold placeholders only

SD-1..SD-3: no upstream name resolves (providers, search, git, fake LLM and SaaS, the app); no TCP to their addresses; through the proxy with the placeholder every upstream is refused and both gateways answer

SG: the tools placeholder lists only granted tools; ungranted tools, servers, toolsets, knowledge and the parent's code_task are refused; a stale attempt, another org and a forged token are refused; the model token names only the grant's neutral model; after the run both are refused and none is minted; a finished job's placeholder reaches no gateway
assert_effects: SK-4: the scripted model received the org's key and the fake SaaS the MCP token, header, OAuth token, SearXNG's key and Jira's token, none from a sandbox's address; no non-model credential reached the model
assert_audit: refusals are logged with their run id and carry no token or credential

scenarios.title: R32-TRUST: at the production floor (gVisor, no dev override) every release engine is offered and runs, its ACP profiles verified against the stack's own test root; an untrusted profile reads "not signed for this deployment", never "not installed"
steps: Bring a human-style stack up with E2E_SANDBOX_RUNTIME=runsc: run.sh signs the tree's ACP profiles with a fresh test key (scripts/engines/sign_vendor_rules.py --test-root, private half never written) and mounts the root read-only as PIPESHUB_TEST_TRUST_ROOT; PIPESHUB_ACP_PROFILES_UNSIGNED and PIPESHUB_ENGINES_WITHOUT_GVISOR are false.
Run smoke_human.py, then journeys.py --tier gate, whose owner_pinned groups pin each ACP engine (acp-opencode, acp-gemini, acp-goose, acp-qwen, acp-dsh).
expect_user: Every engine is a choice on the coding-engine pickers; each ACP job ends with its answer, its approvals, cancel, delete, budget and tool results as on the native engines.

Where a profile is untrusted (no test root, no release signature), the engine is listed greyed with "This engine's profile isn't signed for this deployment" (10 locales), and a save is refused with the same words.
assert_journal: The broker logs enginesUntrusted=[] at start and lists no engine under enginesUnavailable; every job's sandbox runs on runsc.
assert_effects: No unsigned profile is read: a profile changed after signing, or a signature by another key, installs nothing (test_r32_profile_trust.py).
assert_audit: A release build with PIPESHUB_TEST_TRUST_ROOT and without PIPESHUB_ALLOW_TEST_TRUST_ROOT=true does not start (ProfileTestRootRefused).

scenarios.title: R38-IDENT (SEC-C-03, ADR-SLACKID-01): a Slack person acts only as the PipesHub account they linked; a spoofed profile email, a Slack Connect outsider, a guest and a shared channel are refused privately with no lookup
steps: Bring a human-style stack up (E2E_FAKE_SLACK=1, the default of human-up) with E2E_SANDBOX_RUNTIME=runsc.

Run journeys.py on any surface.slack journey: its setup runs slack_identity_holds (a member whose Slack profile email is the admin's, a member of another team, a guest, and the admin in a channel shared with another organisation each mention the bot), then link_slack_person for the admin and the member through the sign-in link the bot sent each of them privately.
expect_user: Each refused person gets a private reply saying plainly that this Slack account cannot use PipesHub here and what to do; nothing is answered in the channel.
An unlinked member gets a private sign-in link; the /slack/link page names both accounts before Approve, and after it the member's mentions are answered as them.
assert_journal: No conversation or run is started for a refused event, and none under the spoofed email's account.
assert_effects: The binding is stored by Slack team id + user id; changing the Slack profile email does not move it; a disabled or deleted PipesHub account loses it at its next use (r38-slack-identity.test.ts).
assert_audit: A link token is single-use, expires after 10 minutes and is bound to its team, user and bot: a replay, an expired token or another team's token links nothing.

steps: bash deployment/docker-compose/tests/store_auth_test.sh (through $PXH_LANE when set): Redis, etcd and Kafka from the real docker-compose.yml, an etcd volume written by the old plain-HTTP etcd.
bash deployment/docker-compose/tests/installer_test.sh: an older .env reused, with and without a public URL.
A human-up stack (its own Redis) comes up with STORE_AUTH_CHECK enforcing and passes smoke_human.py.

scenarios.title: R43-AUTH (R41OPS-FU-7, R41OPS-FU-8, ADR-WEB-02): the web session survives a reload and a new tab with no token in page storage, an older build's localStorage tokens move to the HttpOnly cookie, and the unauthenticated health routes name no store
steps: On a human-up stack, the authenticated Playwright project runs frontend/tests/e2e/auth/session-persistence.spec.ts and auth/logout.spec.ts.
curl -s /api/v1/health and /api/v1/health/services without a token; the same with the admin's token.
smoke_human.py and run.sh wait_capabilities read agentHarness.capabilities from the public answer.
expect_user: A person who signed in stays signed in after a reload, in a second tab and after the upgrade from a build that kept tokens in localStorage; clearing the browser's cookies signs them out.
assert_journal: No run is started by the spec.
assert_effects: After sign-in localStorage and sessionStorage hold no jwt_* key and no JWT-shaped value; the session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict (__Host-, Secure, Path=/ over https); the unauthenticated /api/v1/health answers only status and agentHarness {status, capabilities}, /api/v1/health/services only status and the product services; the admin's token gets the full reports.
assert_audit: A refresh or sign-out that sends the cookie from another origin, or without an Origin, is refused 403.

scenarios.title: R44-IDENT (R43AUTH-FU-1, ADR-WEB-02 D9): every refresh replaces the refresh token; two tabs refreshing together stay signed in; a replayed old cookie ends that sign-in and is audited
steps: On a human-up stack, sign in in the browser; copy the session cookie's value (DevTools or the Playwright context) as the 'old' cookie.
Open a second tab and reload both at once; wait for the proactive refresh in each.
Wait more than 60 seconds, then POST /api/v1/userAccount/refresh/token from a fresh context with the old cookie and this server's Origin.
Reload the original tab; as an admin, search the audit log for identity.session_replayed.
expect_user: Both tabs stay signed in through simultaneous refreshes; after the old cookie is replayed the person is asked to sign in again on that device only.
assert_journal: No run is started.
assert_effects: Each refresh answers a new Set-Cookie value with the same expiry; the replay answers 401 and clears the cookie; the family's next refresh with the newest cookie is also 401; a desktop or bearer refresh gets refreshToken in the body.
assert_audit: One identity.session_replayed entry on the org's audit chain for that sign-in (account and family id, no token, no address); auth.session_replay_detected in the app log.
